title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not about motives. It is page 47 of a typed course on analytic functions of several variables over K (R or C), filed in this folder; the neighbouring handwritten pages on Deuring-type categories and Gr-categories are unrelated.

The page completes a preceding remark: if g is holomorphic, then the integral of dg vanishes along every closed path (circuit) in A.

Proposition 2: let A ⊂ K^n be a contractible domain and ω = Σ f_k dx_k a closed 1-form with holomorphic coefficients. Then ω = dg for some g holomorphic on A.

Lemma 1: any two points a, b of a domain (connected open set) can be joined inside A by a piecewise-linear path. The proof is the standard open-closed argument. Let B be the set of endpoints of piecewise-linear paths in A starting at a. Take c in the closure of B and a ball S around c inside A. S contains a point b of B. The segment from b to c, and every segment from b to a point x of S, lies in S. Hence c ∈ B and S ⊂ B, so B is both open and closed, and therefore equals A.

The proof of the proposition then begins. Fix a and z in A and take two paths γ on [b,c] and γ' from a to z. Reparametrise γ' to lie on [c,d]. Concatenating γ with γ' reversed, γ''(t) = γ'(c+d−t), gives a closed path. So the two integrals agree by an earlier theorem ("th. 3"), presumably the vanishing of integrals of closed forms over circuits in contractible domains, i.e. homotopy invariance. One then defines g(z) = ∫_a^z ω; holomorphy and dg = ω follow on later pages.

This is the standard Poincaré lemma for holomorphic 1-forms, for path integrals.
errors: 'd'origine A' should read 'd'origine a' (the origin is the point a, not the domain A).
'S ⊂ C' and 'C est ouvert et fermé' should read 'S ⊂ B' and 'B est ouvert et fermé': the letter C collides with the point c.
The proof needs the trivial check that B is nonempty (a ∈ B). The open-closed argument shows c ∈ B and S ⊂ B at once, so it gives closedness and openness together; this is fine but tersely stated.

ideas.what: A closed holomorphic 1-form on a contractible (more generally simply connected) domain in K^n has a holomorphic primitive.
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré lemma / exactness of closed holomorphic 1-forms on simply connected domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Cauchy, Poincaré); textbook material (e.g. Cartan, Théorie élémentaire des fonctions analytiques)
ideas.where_published: Not as such; standard textbook result

ideas.what: Connected open subsets of K^n are piecewise-linearly path connected, proved by an open-closed argument.
Independence of a path integral from the path via concatenation with a reversed path to form a circuit.
ideas.modern_name: path independence of line integrals of closed forms

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary typed course page (holomorphic Poincaré lemma, polygonal connectedness of domains), probably misfiled among the motives notes. It contains nothing new or unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: 'route a-chevée' as typed: likely 'route achevée' (closed or finished path) or a typing artefact; the meaning is a piecewise-linear path.
In the final line, the handwritten insertion over γ''(b) is 'a =' (likely with an asterisk), giving γ''(d) = γ'(c) = a = γ''(b).
Marginal '28' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
